title: The intercepted photo
html:
At 23:41 the police intercepted a photo, sent from an unknown phone to an art dealer they have been watching. It shows a crate in a dark shipping container.

Exhibit PDU/06intercepted.jpgthe photo the police interceptedDownload

The picture shows little. The file says more: read its metadata.

prev_card.title: The crate left the building
prev_card.html:
CR-017, with the Mona Lisa, was going to D-01, conservation storage. WS-02 sent it to D-03, the external loading dock. It left at 20:52:10 without a carrier: no transport company was booked.

The data term: API

An API is an address that returns data instead of a page. Change one part of the address, here the crate ID, and you get another record. Apps use APIs all the time: a weather app asks a weather API, a train app asks the railway's API.

fields.label: Where was the photo taken? Give the coordinates or the postcode.
fields.help: <button type="button" class="how" data-howto="map">How to: find a position on a map</button>

hints: On a Mac: open the photo in Preview, then Tools > Show Inspector and the tab with the (i). The Exif tab names the camera, the GPS tab gives the position. Use the downloaded file, not a screenshot.

Copy the position from the GPS tab, for example 49° 28' 3" N and the longitude after it, and paste it in the search box of Google Maps. The pin shows the place. Click it for the address with its postcode.
A Google Pixel 7. Position: 49° 28' 3" N, 0° 9' 45" E, in decimals 49.4675, 0.1625: the Terminal de Normandie in the port of Le Havre, postcode 76610.
